title: Auto Loans: Full-Settlement Figure and Available Balance
content:
This rule states, for an Auto Loans account closed by transfer from the borrower's PCB checking account, the figure needed to pay the loan off in full, how that figure divides, and when the transfer can go ahead.

## Rule

The full-settlement figure is the capital balance, plus the interest owed to the credit date, plus the fees due, plus any prepayment charge, rounded to the cent. The payment divides into a fees share equal to those fees due, an interest share equal to that interest, and a principal share equal to the capital balance.

The transfer can use only money already posted to a checking account of the borrower's that is active. If that account's ledger balance is lower than the full-settlement figure, nothing is posted to close the loan and the sum is 0.00; otherwise the sum drawn is the full-settlement figure.

## Condition, judgement, outcome

| Ledger balance of the active checking account | Sum posted |
|---|---|
| lower than the full-settlement figure | 0.00, and the loan is not closed |
| equal to it or higher | the full-settlement figure |

## Worked example (invented figures)

Capital balance 12389.45, interest to the credit date 57.34, fees due 25.00, no prepayment charge: the full-settlement figure is 12471.79, split as 25.00 to fees, 57.34 to interest and 12389.45 to principal. A ledger balance of 12471.79 or more allows the transfer; a ledger balance of 12000.00 does not, and 0.00 is the sum.
